Orca: the fix stage (Run wf_dabe0930-23d) ended BLOCKED at cc-sync/cross-machine-recovery 0682b92c77.
Done in that stage:
- merged the root fixes;
- D2, D7 (completeness.code_captured_at) and D12b done with tests, including a divergence-prompt render test;
- 19 of 21 review findings fixed with tests, among them a claimed record lost on persistence failure (snapshot rollback), local import landing in a remote partition, the mobile/activation dormant launch, headless `this`, provenance-before-success, the duplicate-dormant replay race, stale client layouts, an SSH tab blocking a local resume, and stderr cap edge cases.
Open: C3 and C12. The stage started before the coordinator decisions were appended to the contract, so it never saw them.
The coordinator stopped the workflow as QA was starting (no QA changes existed) so QA would not test a known-broken Resume.
Replacement Run wf_1a8cd60d-b5c (orca-finish, same branch/worktree):
- C3 decision (b): dormant recovery panes start no PTY; the placeholder offers Resume (fresh launch with requireFreshPane → recovery_placement_occupied, never adopting a shell) and "Start shell instead" (explicit release).
- C12 decision (a): a per-method frame budget for crossMachineRecovery.import only.
- C7 crash-window replay.
- Closing the C8 residual hold window.
- All locale catalogs.
- D1 resolved: recoveryLaunch.appendSystemPrompt → `--append-system-prompt` only when the host's claude advertises it; capability cross-machine-recovery.recovery-launch.v1.
- Then a whole-diff astra review with 2 lenses, a fix pass, and the full hidden rendered QA (ORCA_BACKGROUND_LAUNCH=1): picker spec with env-scrub assertions and screenshots including the divergence prompt; a two-profile export/import e2e with recoveryLaunch, placeholder no-PTY checks, Resume and Start-shell actions, and replay idempotence; the rendered QA tool.
